summary.prose: File and repository entity reads will use transactional secondary indexes instead of scanning every stored entity. A one-time atomic migration derives both indexes from the existing rows, with no reindex required. Existing read results and entity identities stay unchanged, while repository-readiness checks request only a first match.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Reading the entities of one file or one repository scans the whole entity table

dataModelChanges.details: Add entityByFile and entityByRepo dupsort handles in src/db/graph/store.ts. entity_by_file key is SHA256 over the exact UTF-8 absolute path produced by the existing toAbsolutePath representation; entity_by_repo key is repoId u32 BE; both values are entity u64 BE. Verify candidate file/repo equality against authoritative rows, so a digest collision cannot change query correctness. Ensure maxDbs includes the new handles. Registered root paths are identity; a future root relocation must rebuild derived file keys.

Each authoritative entity row has exactly its file-key/u64 and repoId/u64 memberships. Reconcile memberships in every upsert, identity/path move, reindex, embedding rewrite and delete transaction; remove them on file/repo cascade deletes. Inventory all production entity.put/remove sites, including historical migrations. Prior migrations run before v6 backfill; v6 is rebuilt from their final authoritative rows. Preserve strict registration and existing names/edges/vector behavior.

Preserve the two-argument listEntitiesForRepo result; add only the literal first-match option limit:1 for nonempty checks in scope.ts and invariants.ts. Their injectable seams gain an optional argument, so existing injected one-argument functions remain compatible. The code-review per-file watermark uses indexed file entities instead of scanning store.entity directly.

Bump schema 5 to 6 and register an atomic backfill. Fresh stores open empty indexes at v6. A migration error leaves v5 authoritative data and version unchanged, refuses service startup, and can be retried; no silent scan fallback or destructive auto-rebuild. Update current-version assertions in the three cited tests to schema 6; retain explicitly historical v4/v5 migration fixtures and assertions at their named historical versions. Inventory all SCHEMA_VERSION and readSchemaVersion assertions before build.

errorCases.scenario: Entity row or index membership cannot be written.
errorCases.detection: LMDB child transaction throws during row/index reconciliation.
errorCases.response: Abort the entire transaction; expose the existing write error. Do not leave a committed row without its new memberships.
errorCases.userImpact: A write fails visibly rather than creating silently incomplete search results.

errorCases.scenario: Backfill fails or the process exits during migration.
errorCases.detection: Migration transaction throws or never commits schema version 6.
errorCases.response: Leave authoritative v5 data/version intact and refuse serving; retry migration on next open. Do not delete/reindex the store automatically.
errorCases.userImpact: Startup fails with actionable migration diagnostics; user data is preserved.

errorCases.scenario: An index entry refers to a missing authoritative row.
errorCases.detection: Exact-key candidate lookup cannot load its u64 row or mapping.
errorCases.response: Report index/store inconsistency instead of returning a seemingly complete empty result or falling back to a whole-table scan.
errorCases.userImpact: Corruption is visible and cannot masquerade as absence.

errorCases.scenario: Newer schema is opened by an older binary.
errorCases.detection: Existing schema-version preflight sees stored version greater than supported.
errorCases.response: Preserve the existing mismatch refusal. Rollback requires a backup or a binary supporting v6, not a silent schema downgrade.
errorCases.userImpact: Older code cannot mutate incompatible indexes.

errorCases.scenario: An entity references an unregistered repository.
errorCases.detection: Existing registry lookup cannot resolve repo membership during write or backfill.
errorCases.response: Preserve UnregisteredRepoError/write refusal; during migration report and fail rather than allocating a registry row.
errorCases.userImpact: The strict repo.add contract remains intact.

edgeCases.input: Empty registered repo or absent file.
edgeCases.expected: Return existing empty results using exact-key reads; first-match mode returns an empty array without enumerating the table.

edgeCases.input: Unicode or long paths, nested repositories, and equivalent digest keys.
edgeCases.expected: Use the exact prior absolute-path representation for the hash, verify authoritative path equality, preserve every matching row and u64 order, and never use containment as a substitute for equality.

edgeCases.input: Entity moves file or repository but keeps its u64 in a write.
edgeCases.expected: Remove the old memberships and insert the new ones atomically; no duplicates or stale results.

edgeCases.input: Repeated identical upsert or embedding-only rewrite.
edgeCases.expected: Membership updates are idempotent and cannot duplicate an entity or lose an existing membership.
Index enumeration and row resolution use a consistent LMDB read snapshot; results describe one state, never partially updated membership.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Two-argument scoped reads preserve current returned entities and u64 iteration order; s1 symbol and read-fallback bundles.
Entity membership changes share the authoritative write transaction; use the existing name-index reconciliation pattern identified in s1.
Daemon owns DB access, unknown repos are never auto-registered, and migration failure never silently rebuilds user data; s1 store/registry read-fallback.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test via tsx, matching the repository's documented backend/db test command; all storage tests use temporary registered repositories and isolated LMDB paths.

testLevels.purpose: Prove key encoding, exact matching and compatibility.
subjects: File-key hashing is deterministic for the existing absolute-path representation and supports long Unicode paths.
Repository keys and entity-u64 dupsort values preserve isolation and result order.
A forced file-key digest collision still returns only rows with the exact requested absolute path.
fixturesNeeded: Two repos with same relative filenames, long/Unicode paths, deterministic u64 IDs
Internal digest seam for an artificial collision

testLevels.purpose: Prove every entity mutation maintains both indices transactionally.
subjects: Insert, same-ID update, file/repo move, reindex replacement, embedding-only update, delete by ID/file/repo all match an authoritative fixture oracle.
An injected transaction failure rolls back both row and index membership changes.
Compare file/repo reads and grouped file lists to pre-change content/order.
Repository existence requests limit:1 and reads at most the first matching authoritative entity.
Code-review per-file watermark uses indexed file entities.
fixturesNeeded: Isolated LMDB environment registered exclusively through existing repo-add test helpers
Mixed target/unrelated rows with stable expected result arrays

testLevels.purpose: Prove the scoped operations cannot silently regress to whole-table scans.
subjects: After setup/backfill, replace entity.getRange with a throwing spy; file/repo lookups, deletion collectors, file reindex snapshots and readiness checks still work.
Count entity.get calls to show unrelated rows are not read.
Unregistered repo writes remain refused and never create registry rows.
fixturesNeeded: Read-operation spies installed only after fixture creation/migration

testLevels.purpose: Prove v5-to-v6 migration, crash safety and version compatibility.
subjects: Open a populated v5 fixture, backfill on startup and verify exact file/repo results without invoking the indexer.
Inject failure after partial backfill; reopen at version 5 with no partial committed index and retry successfully.
Fresh v6 store starts with empty usable indices; a second reopen does not rebuild them.
Existing unsupported-version refusal remains in force.
Run doc-summary-carry, migration-v4-to-v5 and operational suites: latest-version expectations follow v6, while explicit historical migration fixtures still prove their original transitions.
fixturesNeeded: Populated v5 file containing every row class used by entity queries
Migration failure hook and reopen fixture

provingTests: File lookup and file collectors use exact-key candidates; whole-table read spy throws without affecting the operations.
Repository lookup/file grouping uses only its u64 set and keeps existing content/order.
Mutation matrix and rollback tests prove exact membership after every supported write/delete.
Populated v5 startup migrates once without reindex; failure rolls back and retry succeeds.
Readiness requests only one indexed match; no full repository materialization and no unrelated entity reads.

migration.stateBefore: The s1 analyzer locates SCHEMA_VERSION=5 and whole-table entity.getRange loops in scoped reads and deletion collectors. The existing graph store already uses dupsort secondary indices and runMigrations; file/repo membership indexes are absent.
migration.stateAfter: Schema v6 has exact file/repo dupsort memberships derived from authoritative rows. Scoped reads and collectors use them, and readiness requests a first match. Existing rows, IDs, vectors and registry membership are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the two named DB handles and binary/digest key definitions; verify named-DB capacity before environment open.
Register v5-to-v6 backfill that clears/rebuilds derived memberships from authoritative rows and validates registry roots inside one child transaction, stamping v6 only on success.
Wire every entity write/delete and scoped read to the membership contract, then update the two readiness seams and per-file review watermark.
Validate fresh/populated migration, rollback-on-failure, reopen idempotence, exact result compatibility and no-full-scan spies on temporary environments before any installed-store deployment.

migration.backwardCompat: All existing two-argument scoped-read callers keep the same content and ordering. Only readiness callers opt into the additive limit:1 mode. Persisted v6 is forward-only: an older binary must retain its existing newer-schema refusal. Before deployment preserve a normal store backup; binary rollback after migration requires that backup or a v6-capable binary, not a silent downgrade. No repo re-registration or reindex.

alternativesConsidered.name: Two transactional dupsort secondary indexes
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add exact file and repository entity-ID indexes beside authoritative rows.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Reuse existing LMDB dupsort patterns: file key is a fixed-size digest of the existing absolute-path representation and repository key is repoId; values are big-endian entity u64 IDs. Resolve candidates through authoritative rows and verify exact path/repo equality. Maintain entries atomically with every row write/delete; migrate existing rows once on open. Existing scoped-read APIs retain their results and ordering.
pros: Direct exact-key lookups avoid unrelated entity rows.
Fixed-size file keys handle long Unicode paths; authoritative row filtering keeps digest collisions correct.
No cache invalidation or persistent data loss; dupsort values preserve u64 result order.
cons: Two additional named DBs and migration/write-maintenance work.
Every entity mutation must reconcile old and new keys in its transaction.

alternativesConsidered.name: Repository-only secondary index with file filtering
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Index repository entity IDs and filter those rows for file queries.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add only repoId-to-entity-ID dupsort. Repository reads enumerate that set; file reads select containing registered repositories and filter their indexed entity rows, preserving final path comparison.
pros: One fewer named DB and simpler mutation maintenance.
cons: File queries still scan unrelated files in a large repo, violating the approved defect contract.
Containment selection can miss nonstandard stored file paths unless every repository is inspected.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheaper but still reads other files in the target repository; that fails the core file-scope requirement.

erDefinition.narrative: The new memberships are derived LMDB key/value indexes, not new authoritative entities. Each membership resolves to an existing entity row; the registry remains the source of repository identity.
